message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Below is an overview of key rights you typically enjoy as a renter: | Category | Typical Tenant Rights (Texas) | Notes | |----------|------------------------------|-------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Landlords must itemize deductions and provide receipts if requested. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain premises in a safe, sanitary condition; repair structural defects, plumbing, heating, electrical, etc.
• Must keep common areas clean and safe. | If landlord fails, tenants may withhold rent, repair & deduct, or terminate lease. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without notice (usually 24‑hour written notice unless emergency).
• Landlord must respect privacy. | Exceptions: emergencies, repairs, inspections with proper notice. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day notice to pay or vacate.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month agreements; 60‑day for longer leases. | Notice must be in writing and delivered personally or via certified mail. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Protected classes: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, source of income, etc.
• Fair Housing Act applies to all housing. | Discriminatory practices include refusing to rent, setting higher rents, or imposing different terms. | | **Repair & Deduct / Withhold Rent** | • If landlord fails to fix major problems, tenant may repair and deduct cost from rent or withhold rent until fixed. | Must follow proper procedure: give notice, allow reasonable time to fix, document costs. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing for >1 year.
• Certain clauses (e.g., “no pets” or “no smoking”) are enforceable only if they comply with local ordinances. | Some local rules may override or add to state law. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve a valid notice (pay or vacate, cure or quit, etc.).
• Eviction requires court action; unlawful detainer suit. | Tenants can contest eviction in court; may file for relief if eviction is retaliatory or discriminatory. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has no statewide rent control; local ordinances may apply in certain cities. | Check city ordinances for restrictions on rent increases. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide hot water, heat, and electricity unless otherwise specified.
• Landlord may require tenant to pay utilities if stated in lease. | Verify utility responsibilities in lease. | ### Practical Steps If You Encounter Problems 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of lease, notices, emails, photos of damage, repair requests, and receipts. 2. **Give Written Notice** – Send a written request for repairs or a notice of intent to withhold rent if necessary. 3. **Check Local Ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional tenant protection laws. 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If disputes arise, consult a local attorney or tenant advocacy group. Many nonprofits offer free or low‑cost legal assistance. --- #### Want a Sample Lease? If you’re drafting or reviewing a lease, I can help generate a sample Texas residential lease tailored to your situation. Just let me know the type of property (single‑family, apartment, etc.), the parties involved, and any special provisions you’d like to include.
